props.title: Plunkett & Macleane
props.initialSlug: Two rogues become London's most dashing highwaymen

sections.content: Plunkett & Macleane (1999) represents a bold, stylistic departure from traditional period pieces, blending 18th-century highwayman drama with modern sensibilities. Director Jake Scott (son of Ridley Scott) infused contemporary music, kinetic editing, and a punk rock attitude into this Georgian-era crime caper. The film pairs Jonny Lee Miller and Robert Carlyle as unlikely partners-in-crime, following the real historical template of gentleman robber James MacLean while taking significant creative liberties. Like A Knight's Tale (2001) and Marie Antoinette (2006), it deliberately anachronistic approach divided critics but developed a cult following.

sections.content: The film's unique visual style owes much to the late-90s aesthetic that also influenced Shakespeare in Love (1998) and Sleepy Hollow (1999). Cinematographer John Mathieson, who would later lens Gladiator (2000), created a grimy yet glamorous version of 1748 London. The film's notorious party sequences, scored to contemporary electronic music, established a template for period pieces with modern soundtracks that would influence everything from Sofia Coppola's Marie Antoinette (2006) to The Great (2020).

While commercially unsuccessful upon release, Plunkett & Macleane has gained appreciation for its pioneering style fusion. The chemistry between Miller and Carlyle echoes classic buddy criminal partnerships like those in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid (1969), while the film's class warfare themes and Robin Hood elements resonate with modern audiences. The supporting cast includes Alan Cumming and Ken Stott delivering memorable character work that grounds the more experimental elements. SUBHEAD: Impact on Period Action Films

sections.content: The film's influence can be seen in later period action pieces that weren't afraid to take creative liberties with history. Brotherhood of the Wolf (2001) similarly mixed period setting with martial arts action, while The Three Musketeers (2011) adopted comparable stylistic flourishes. Even serious historical dramas like The Favourite (2018) owe something to Plunkett & Macleane's irreverent approach to period storytelling.
